cases.name: 01_ClothesWeekend
cases.contentsAnswer: Clothes for the weekend and a wash bag. No equipment.
cases.weightAnswer: About five or six kilos including the suitcase.
cases.metalAnswer: Just the zip, handle and small toiletry fittings.
cases.packingAnswer: Everything is folded tightly between straps.
cases.responseAnswer: Nothing loose or powered. It should barely move.
cases.authorReasoning: Low metal, 5.4 kg and fixed balance support all statements. Straightforward innocent.

cases.name: 02_MechanicTools
cases.contentsAnswer: Workshop tools and padding. I am repairing a truck tomorrow.
cases.weightAnswer: Nearly fifteen kilos with the hard case. Yes, it is heavy.
cases.metalAnswer: Steel spanners, sockets and a hammer; a strong metal response is expected.
cases.packingAnswer: The tray is not latched; it can slide a little downhill.
cases.responseAnswer: A short metal rattle. Once the tray settles, it should stay on that side.
cases.authorReasoning: Heavy and metal-rich is legitimate. Tilt shifts downhill; leveling preserves tray displacement. No active recovery.

cases.name: 03_BooksAndCamera
cases.contentsAnswer: Several books, a camera and a spare shirt.
cases.weightAnswer: Around nine kilos. The books are most of it.
cases.metalAnswer: An old metal-bodied camera, wrapped between the books.
cases.responseAnswer: No battery motor or loose mechanism. A small dull impact is possible.
cases.authorReasoning: 9.2 kg and modest metal response fit a metal camera among heavier books; fixed balanced load.

cases.name: 04_WaterAndLaundry
cases.contentsAnswer: Laundry and a sealed water jug for my camping trip.
cases.weightAnswer: About ten kilos; most of it is water.
cases.metalAnswer: Plastic bottles and fabric. Very little metal apart from the zip.
cases.packingAnswer: The jug is strapped down, but water can move inside.
cases.responseAnswer: A slosh after shaking. It will settle back when the platform is level.
cases.authorReasoning: Liquid response is innocent: downhill offset under tilt, level balance recovers, long decay. Claims acknowledge liquid.

cases.name: 05_ForgottenTripod
cases.contentsAnswer: Mainly clothes. I packed in a hurry.
cases.weightAnswer: Maybe six kilos... I did not weigh it.
cases.metalAnswer: You are right: my camera tripod is still in the side pocket. I forgot it.
cases.packingAnswer: The tripod is strapped on the right; the clothes hold it still.
cases.responseAnswer: There are no loose parts; the tripod clamps are locked.
cases.authorReasoning: Initial mass estimate is wrong but follow-up explains metal and stable right-heavy balance. An honest omission, not a universal lie detector.

cases.name: 06_PrivateWeights
cases.contentsAnswer: Only some clothes and personal things.
cases.weightAnswer: All right, there are exercise weights under the clothes. Roughly sixteen kilos total.
cases.metalAnswer: The weights are cast metal. I did not want to explain my training equipment.
cases.packingAnswer: One weight is loose at the bottom. It slides downhill, then stays there.
cases.responseAnswer: A heavy short thud, perhaps some metal rattle. Nothing can push back uphill.
cases.authorReasoning: Deliberately misleading innocent. Follow-ups predict high mass/metal and passive irreversible sliding. False accusation remains possible.

cases.name: 07_WoundMusicMechanism
cases.contentsAnswer: A spring-driven music mechanism for restoration. No batteries.
cases.weightAnswer: About eight kilos including the protective case.
cases.metalAnswer: Brass gears, steel springs and the carrying case hardware.
cases.packingAnswer: It is mounted on a moving suspension. The spring is still wound.
cases.responseAnswer: It can react after a short delay and pull its counterweight back. That is why I said spring-driven, not an empty box.
cases.authorReasoning: Counter-motion and delayed response have a legitimate disclosed clockwork cause, supported by metal-rich load. Same response vocabulary as some Mimics.

cases.name: 08_PoweredCameraRig
cases.contentsAnswer: A camera stabilizer with a battery fitted, wrapped in pads.
cases.weightAnswer: Just under nine kilos including the suitcase.
cases.metalAnswer: The metal frame, camera and battery account for a moderate reading.
cases.packingAnswer: The rig is powered. I forgot the transport lock, so it tries to stay centered.
cases.responseAnswer: It can correct against a tilt and move after a short delay. I should have turned it off.
cases.authorReasoning: Innocent powered counterbalance. Mass and metal agree; the guest admits power and unlocked mechanism. Counter-motion alone is not conclusive.

cases.name: 09_LightClothesCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: A few light clothes and a towel. Nothing else.
cases.weightAnswer: Four or five kilos, certainly no heavy equipment.
cases.metalAnswer: No tools or electronics; just the suitcase fittings.
cases.packingAnswer: Everything is tightly strapped. Nothing loose.
cases.responseAnswer: That movement must be the clothes settling. There is no mechanism.
cases.authorReasoning: 13 kg contradicts the confident light-load claim. Counterbalance/delayed pulse contradict both fixed packing and passive cloth. At least two independent clues.

cases.name: 10_FalseToolboxCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: A full case of steel spanners and sockets.
cases.weightAnswer: About eleven kilos, a normal tool kit.
cases.metalAnswer: It should be mostly metal: steel tools fill almost all the case.
cases.packingAnswer: The trays are bolted down. The heavy part is on the left.
cases.responseAnswer: Any sound is steel against steel. There is no spring or suspension.
cases.authorReasoning: Mass is plausible but metal response around 9 percent is incompatible with mostly steel. Elastic recovery also contradicts bolted trays. No need for universal counter-motion cue.

cases.name: 11_UnsecuredRadioCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Books and an old radio. I left the radio unsecured.
cases.weightAnswer: About ten or eleven kilos with the backpack.
cases.metalAnswer: The radio has a metal cover; the books are paper.
cases.packingAnswer: The radio may slide. It is unplugged and the batteries are removed.
cases.responseAnswer: Any movement is just the loose radio falling downhill. There is no wound spring or motor.
cases.authorReasoning: Initial mass/metal are plausible. Left and right tilts show motion against the slope, followed by delayed pulse recovery. An unpowered loose radio cannot explain the combination.

cases.name: 12_LockedGimbalCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Camera equipment and padding. It includes a stabilizer.
cases.weightAnswer: About thirteen kilos with the suitcase.
cases.metalAnswer: Some metal brackets and lenses, not a full metal tool kit.
cases.packingAnswer: The battery is removed and the transport pin locks the moving stage solid.
cases.responseAnswer: It cannot move by itself while pinned. A small vibration is just the foam.
cases.authorReasoning: Plausible technically true cover story. Packing follow-up asserts a locked stage; opposing tilt response and delayed sizable movement contradict that. Compare innocent powered rig, whose explanation differs.

cases.name: 13_StaticSamplesCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: Nonmetallic sample weights and foam. They are packed in a centered rigid block.
cases.weightAnswer: About twelve kilos total. Nothing lightweight.
cases.packingAnswer: The single block is fixed exactly in the center, evenly padded left and right.
cases.responseAnswer: Nothing should move. The block cannot shift in its housing.
cases.authorReasoning: A quiet, braced Mimic has no signature sound or counter-motion. Stable left-heavy center of mass around -4.2 cm contradicts the explicit centered symmetrical packing. Weight and metal alone would miss it.

cases.name: 14_PackedBatteryCarrier
cases.contentsAnswer: A small battery and hand tools, all fitted in solid foam.
cases.weightAnswer: Eight kilos or so with the case.
cases.metalAnswer: There is metal in the tools and battery, but lots of packing as well.
cases.packingAnswer: No liquid containers. All the fitted pieces are clamped and cannot slide.
cases.responseAnswer: A slight rattle from a loose latch, nothing with a long moving response.
cases.authorReasoning: Mass/metal plausible. Large tilt displacement, level recovery and delayed long pulse decay contradict both solid clamps and no liquid/moving mechanism. Different combination from low-metal toolbox or quiet off-center case.
